closed_form.provenance: Computed. Closed-form integer arithmetic over a descriptor plus per-rate base and slope tables.

morph.provenance: Computed from user-set endpoints. Emulator X only; absent from the Proteus 2000 ROM filter table.

rom_table.provenance: Stored. A table read with no arithmetic on the words.

law.note: Radius is an affine function of frequency. Morph Designer's rad = ((freq * 0x7c) >> 8) + 0x76 is the same law with different constants: in word units 440*byte + 4608 against 442*byte + 4896. Neither compiler carries a per-section volume term; the shared writer emits the constant 0xdfff as the fifth word.

phantom_classes.mapping_basis: Filter names are matched to classes by order and type, which is unambiguous for the pole-count and EQ classes. BlissBatz to CPhantomBatman is positional: it is the remaining entry in the PhazeShift1/PhazeShift2/BlissBatz/FlangerLite run, which the dispatch table holds in the same order as Phaser1/Phaser2/Batman/Flanger1.
phantom_classes.source: EmulatorX.dll (Emulator X3, 2008-09-14). Filter-class dispatch table at 0x1806d5f80, 32-byte records; class names are the MSVC RTTI names reached through each record's descriptor pointer. Within a record the descriptor belongs to the compile function of the following record; that one-record shift is verified at both ends of the table, by CPhantomFilterP2k resolving to FUN_1802d3ce0 (the bank reader named in ghidra_extracts/runtime_hacks.md) and CPhantomLP2Pole to FUN_1802c4b80.

members.sentence: Classic analog sweeping with hot Q and Lo-end.

members.name: KlubKlassik
members.sentence: Responsive low-pass filter sweep with a wide spectrum of Q sounds

members.name: BassTracer
members.sentence: Low Q boosts bass. Try sawtooth or square waveform with Q set to 115.

members.name: RogueHertz
members.sentence: Bass with mid-range boost and smooth Q. Sweep cutoff with Q at 127.

members.name: RazorBlades
members.sentence: Cuts a series of frequency bands. Q selects different bands.

members.sentence: Band limited for a cheap radio-like EQ

members.name: Eeh-To-Aah
members.sentence: "E" to "Ah" formant movement. Q accentuates "peakiness."

members.name: UbuOrator
members.sentence: Aah-Uuh vowel with no Q. Raise Q for throaty vocals.

members.name: DeepBouche
members.sentence: French vowels! "Ou-Est" vowel at low Q.

members.sentence: Phasey movement. Try major 6 interval and maximum Q.

members.name: DeadRinger
members.sentence: Permanent "Ringy" Q response. Many Q variations.

members.name: ZoomPeaks
members.sentence: High resonance nasal filter

members.name: AcidRavage
members.sentence: Great analog Q response. Wide tonal range. Try with a sawtooth LFO.

members.name: BassOMatic
members.sentence: Low boost for basslines. Q goes to distortion at the maximum level.

members.name: LucifersQ

members.name: ToothComb
members.sentence: Highly resonant harmonic peaks shift in unison. Try mid Q.
